# NI05 bounded holder completion and cached delivery

Status: partial source implementation on the service worktree, not installed execution authority. The private request-only completion path accepts exact request bytes and a compact holder proof. It inspects an untrusted retained row, then reacquires actual Wallet, Native policy and issuer-key owners in order. The holder signature is authenticated before private issuer-key acquisition. The expected Wallet policy is derived independently from the actual current delegation reference and the prepared Native receiver policy, never from submitted proof fields.

All original claims, raw bytes, evidence observations and lineage must match the retained challenge under the current policy. The concrete guard strictly verifies holder and issuer signatures, constructs the existing Packet v0 and schema-4 context, preserves the original issue/expiry window and records actual verification/signing times separately. The cached path validates the exact stored signed bytes under fresh current owners without signing again or renewing expiry. Final unique journal export repeats the complete guard after durable commit and SQLite close while retaining the actual owner and journal locks.

An exact cached request invalidated before journal admission receives negative-only cleanup after partial owners drop. Cleanup compares the exact completed packet/context/event times under lock, uses the same sticky clock and never substitutes a successful result for the original denial. Cleanup storage/clock uncertainty remains a denial; it is not proof that a tombstone persisted. Mismatching proof/request bytes do not reject an unrelated legitimate cache. Journal-returned errors receive no outer retry or second cleanup. Ambiguous retained requests deny at inspection and final locked export.

This supports only descriptors with no external evidence, credential, capability or authority-mode obligations; every nonempty obligation still denies. Empty context summaries attest no external evidence. Generic caller v1, human Wallet, Packet v0, context schema 4, existing journal storage and legacy denied authority ports stay compatible. Current Wallet source can sign fixed holder proofs, but cross-component immutable composition, trusted CLI/provider startup, result attestation, direct Mac target admission and the live pilot remain unfinished. No VM is mandatory, and this checkpoint requires no cloud upload or further storage cleanup.

Final ordinary-source validation passes **1,040 workspace tests, zero failures and one existing opt-in workflow ignore**, including all 31 authority checks. Workspace build, strict all-target Clippy and formatting pass. All 327 source files remained unchanged during these final checks. The existing ignore requires a selected Wallet binary and isolated Devgraph workflow fixtures; it is not a VM requirement. Known failed attempts remain retained: the missing-method TDD red, a borrowed-clock refactor compile error, a test-only digest-helper call caught by ordinary-library checks, and four unnecessary test adapter drops caught by strict lint. The final code changes neither clock semantics nor authority denials to make these pass.

## Validation boundary

Ordinary disposable public fixture tests exercise both Runtime and Service. They use known public issuer/holder test seeds and actual temporary filesystem/journal locks. They do not certify actual Wallet private seed health, the coupled administrative crash matrix, installed enrolment or live provider admission. The ordinary Wallet holder package has separate real-current-custody/real-clock source evidence; composing those components is a subsequent step.

The receiver wire remains exact bincode Packet v0 and SignedVerifiedCallContext schema 4. Context replay_scope is `session:opcode:nonce`; descriptor fingerprints retain `descriptor:sha256:`. No caller-built packet/context/policy/time/key is accepted by this private producer. Existing receiver helper/SDK guards continue to verify exact raw bytes, selected public issuer, audience, original expiry, current permissions and replay at dispatch. This source checkpoint does not exercise an installed receiver invocation.
